tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
The recorded session shows a complete Magento 1.9 admin flow:
1) Navigate directly to the catalog product admin URL.
2) Encounter the login page, input provided credentials (admin/password123), and submit the form to log in.
3) Land on the Manage Products grid (catalog_product/index), with mass actions, filters, row checkboxes, and pagination.
4) Analyze page structure via extraction to understand grid columns, filters, selection links (Select All/Visible, Unselect All/Visible), mass action dropdown, Status dropdown (for Change status), and Submit button.
5) Demonstrate selection of individual products using row checkboxes.
6) Demonstrate Change status bulk operation:
   - Choose mass action "Change status" from the Actions dropdown.
   - Choose status "Disabled" from the Status dropdown.
   - Click Submit to apply, page reloads with success message.
7) Demonstrate Select Visible to bulk-select all 20 visible products via the selection link.
8) Demonstrate Delete mass action:
   - After Select Visible (20 items selected), choose "Delete" in Actions.
   - Click Submit to trigger delete; page reloads with success message that 20 records were deleted.
9) Demonstrate sorting by clicking the "Name" column header.
10) Demonstrate Update Attributes mass action:
   - Use Select Visible to select products again.
   - Choose "Update Attributes" in Actions.
   - Click Submit to navigate to catalog_product_action_attribute/edit mass-update form.
11) On Update attributes page, analyze structure: attribute rows with labels, Change checkboxes, Meta Title field, Save button.
12) Attempt to input into Meta Title and save (input attempts logged but may not have taken effect due to environment), still giving us stable selectors and indices for the field and Save button.

Task Definition:
The automation tool should:
- Log into Magento admin using fixed credentials.
- Navigate to the Manage Products grid.
- Select products according to a specified selection mode (visible rows via Select Visible or individual row checkboxes by ID/position).
- Apply a chosen mass action: Delete, Change status (Enabled/Disabled), or Update Attributes (specifically Meta Title), using the Actions dropdown and Submit.
- For Update Attributes, navigate to the mass-update form, set Meta Title if provided (ensuring the attribute’s Change toggle is set), and Save.

The previous tool failed because it relied on a deterministic CSS selector (#productGrid_massaction-select) that was not found at runtime in a mis-rendered environment. The new tool must:
- Be robust to timing and rendering issues by using higher-level navigation and agentic discovery for key controls when necessary.
- Avoid hardcoded DOM IDs that may differ across environments.
- Use semantic selectors and, where needed, an agent step to locate controls like the Actions dropdown and Submit button.

Action Plan:
1) Navigation to Admin Grid
   - Use navigation to go directly to the catalog product grid URL: /index.php/admin/catalog_product/.

2) Login (if login form present)
   - Detect login form (username & password inputs, Login button). Here, we have stable element hashes from the demo for username, password, and login button.
   - Input username "admin" and password "password123".
   - Click Login and wait for redirect to admin dashboard or directly to the requested grid.

3) Ensure we are on Manage Products grid
   - If the grid is not immediately visible (blank content), an agentic step may be used to re-navigate or wait. However, the provided environment shows that after login, we land on the grid with URL /admin/catalog_product/index/ or /index/store/0/.
   - For robustness to future variations, we keep the main navigation step to /index.php/admin/catalog_product/ and allow Magento to redirect.

4) Product selection step
   - Support two selection modes based on input parameter selection_mode:
     a) "visible": use the "Select Visible" link above the grid to select all currently visible rows (20 by default).
     b) "checkbox": select a specific set of rows by clicking their per-row checkboxes in the first column, resolved via agentic logic keyed by product IDs or row indices. Given our tools (index-based click) and the demo data, deterministic index-based checkbox selection is brittle; thus for genericity, the tool should prefer the "Select Visible" option for multi-product operations and allow future extension for per-row selection.
   - Because the original goal emphasizes both per-row selection and Select Visible, we demonstrate per-row by at least one checkbox click, and Select Visible for bulk.

5) Choose and execute mass action
   - Using the Actions dropdown in the bulk actions toolbar, select the value provided by the mass_action input parameter: one of "Delete", "Change status", or "Update Attributes".
   - For mass_action = "Change status":
     - Select desired status ("Enabled" or "Disabled") from the Status dropdown (label "Status").
     - Click Submit button in the same toolbar.
   - For mass_action = "Delete":
     - Click Submit; Magento will typically show a JS confirmation dialog. Our execution environment does not expose the confirm dialog, so we assume confirm is accepted automatically or not surfaced. The demo shows the delete succeeded.
   - For mass_action = "Update Attributes":
     - Click Submit and wait until the mass Update attributes form (/catalog_product_action_attribute/edit/) is loaded.

6) Meta Title update on mass-update form (only for mass_action = Update Attributes)
   - On the Update attributes page, locate the "Meta Title" row:
     - Check its "Change" checkbox to mark it as changed.
     - Input the meta_title_value into the Meta Title input text field (if non-empty; if empty, we can still mark Change and leave blank, but typically the caller will pass a value).
   - Click the Save button to apply the update to all selected products.

7) End state
   - After Save, Magento typically returns to the Manage Products grid with a success message about records updated. No further extraction is required.

Variable Identification:
Based on the flows, we need the following input parameters:
1) mass_action (string, required, enum: ["Delete", "Change status", "Update Attributes"])
   - Determines which bulk operation to execute via the Actions dropdown.

2) selection_mode (string, required, enum: ["visible", "checkbox"])
   - "visible": use Select Visible to select all products on the current page.
   - "checkbox": select a single row via its first checkbox (for demo, likely the first visible row). This is more demonstrational; in a real tool it would be extended with product IDs.

3) status_value (string, optional, enum: ["Enabled", "Disabled"])
   - Only used when mass_action = "Change status" to choose the new status.

4) meta_title_value (string, optional)
   - Only used when mass_action = "Update Attributes". Value to input into the Meta Title field on the mass-update form.

5) base_admin_url (string, optional, defaulting conceptually to "http://dockerized-magento.local")
   - While the demo uses a fixed docker host, parameterizing the base allows reuse in other environments. However, our tool infrastructure does not support default values directly; instead, we document that the caller should pass a full catalog product grid URL if needed. To keep the tool simple, we’ll use a single required url_catalog_product input parameter that includes the full grid URL, matching what we navigated to originally.

Thus final inputs:
- url_catalog_product: string (required) – full URL to the Manage Products grid, e.g., "http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/catalog_product/".
- mass_action: string (required, enum: ["Delete", "Change status", "Update Attributes"]).
- selection_mode: string (required, enum: ["visible", "checkbox"]).
- status_value: string (optional, enum: ["Enabled", "Disabled"]) – required logically for Change status, but we mark optional in schema and expect callers to pass it when relevant.
- meta_title_value: string (optional) – used only for Update Attributes.

Step Optimization and Determinism:
- Navigation: Instead of multi-step navigation (admin root -> catalog -> Manage Products), we directly go to url_catalog_product for speed and determinism. Magento will handle redirects (to login, then back).
- Login: We use deterministic input steps targeting the username and password inputs by CSS selectors or element hashes; the screenshot and previous interactions show stable positions. However, because IDs/names aren’t provided, we can rely on an agentic step to locate the username/password inputs by label text ("User Name" and "Password") and enter credentials, increasing robustness across themes.
- Grid interactions: The previous attempt failed using #productGrid_massaction-select, so we avoid hardcoding that ID. Instead, we:
  * Use an agentic step to locate the bulk "Actions" select element by label text "Actions" and visible options containing Delete/Change status/Update Attributes.
  * Use agentic steps to click the "Select Visible" link by its text.
  * Use deterministic steps only where we have both elementHash and consistent tag/role (e.g., Save button on update form, Meta Title input), but we still prefer semantic CSS selectors.
- Update Attributes page: Again, IDs are not shown in the text, so we:
  * Use an agent step to locate the Meta Title row based on label text "Meta Title" (and its Change checkbox), then input meta_title_value.
  * Use agent step to locate and click the Save button by its label.

We include explicit wait steps where the page changes (after login submission, after mass action submission, after navigating to update form) to mitigate timing issues.

Why agent steps are needed:
- The failure log for #productGrid_massaction-select shows that relying on that hard-coded ID is brittle; the element might be absent or differently named (theme customization, grid ID change). Using agent steps that search by label text and option content (Delete/Change status/Update Attributes) is more robust.
- Similarly, the Meta Title input and Change checkbox may not expose stable IDs, but the row label text "Meta Title" is stable.

PASS 2 URL Optimization:
- The core task isn’t purely search/filter via GET parameters; it involves POST-based mass actions and a complex mass-update form. URL manipulation cannot replace the UI interactions in a safe, general way. Therefore, we keep the UI clicks and do not introduce extra URL operations beyond initial navigation.

Summary:
- The tool will: navigate to url_catalog_product, login if necessary, ensure the Manage Products grid is visible, select products either via Select Visible or row checkbox, apply one of the three mass actions, and, for Update Attributes, edit Meta Title and save.
- Inputs are url_catalog_product, mass_action, selection_mode, status_value, and meta_title_value.
- We prioritize agent steps for dynamic controls (Actions dropdown, selection links, grid checkboxes, Meta Title row, Save button) to avoid brittle selectors like #productGrid_massaction-select and address the specific failure seen previously.
name: tool_magento_bulk_product_operations_v2
description: Perform Magento admin bulk product operations (Delete, Change status, Update Attributes including Meta Title) from the Manage Products grid using robust selectors and flows that avoid reliance on #productGrid_massaction-select. Handles login, grid selection (row checkboxes or Select Visible), mass action selection, and optional Meta Title update.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Magento Manage Products grid URL (will redirect to login if not authenticated).
If not already logged in, locate the Magento admin login form, enter fixed credentials (admin / password123), submit, and wait until the Manage Products grid is visible.
steps.task: On the current page, if a login form is present (fields labeled 'User Name' and 'Password' with a 'Login' button), enter username 'admin' and password 'password123', click the Login button, and wait until the Manage Products grid (page titled 'Manage Products' with a product table and Actions dropdown) is displayed. If already on the Manage Products grid, do nothing and proceed.

steps.description: Ensure we are on the Manage Products grid. If not, navigate to the catalog product grid URL and confirm grid visibility.
steps.task: Confirm that the Magento Manage Products grid is visible (look for heading 'Manage Products' and a product grid table with columns like ID, Name, SKU). If the grid is not visible, navigate to '{url_catalog_product}' or the corresponding catalog_product/index URL from the admin menu and wait until the grid is fully loaded.

steps.description: Select products according to selection_mode: either click 'Select Visible' or select at least one row checkbox.
steps.task: On the Manage Products grid, select products for bulk action based on selection_mode. If selection_mode is 'visible', locate and click the 'Select Visible' link above the grid so that the counter shows all visible items selected (e.g., '20 items selected'). If selection_mode is 'checkbox', locate the first few product rows in the grid and click their leftmost selection checkboxes so that at least one item is selected. Verify that the items selected counter is greater than 0.

steps.description: Choose the requested mass action in the Actions dropdown and, for Change status, choose the target status.
steps.task: In the bulk actions toolbar above the product grid, locate the 'Actions' select/dropdown (it has options 'Delete', 'Change status', 'Update Attributes') and set it to the value specified by {mass_action}. If {mass_action} is 'Change status', then locate the 'Status' select control in the same toolbar and set it to {status_value} (either 'Enabled' or 'Disabled').

steps.description: Submit the selected mass action and wait for the result (grid reload, delete confirmation handling, or navigation to Update Attributes form).
steps.task: Click the 'Submit' button in the bulk actions toolbar to execute the current mass action. If a browser confirmation dialog appears for deletion, confirm it. For 'Delete' or 'Change status', wait until the Manage Products grid reloads and shows a success message (e.g., records updated or deleted). For 'Update Attributes', wait until the 'Update attributes' page (catalog_product_action_attribute/edit) loads, showing the mass attribute form.

steps.description: If mass_action is 'Update Attributes' and a Meta Title value is provided, set Meta Title and mark it as changed, then save.
steps.task: If the current page is the 'Update attributes' mass-edit form and {mass_action} is 'Update Attributes', then: 1) Locate the row labeled 'Meta Title'. 2) In that row, ensure the 'Change' checkbox is checked so this attribute will be updated. 3) In the Meta Title input field in the same row, enter the value {meta_title_value} (if {meta_title_value} is non-empty; if it is empty, leave the field as-is but keep the checkbox unchecked). 4) Locate and click the 'Save' button (typically a button with text 'Save' in the header or footer button bar). 5) Wait until Magento navigates back to the Manage Products grid and shows a success message indicating that product attributes have been updated.

input_schema.name: url_catalog_product
input_schema.description: Full URL to the Magento Manage Products grid, e.g. "http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/catalog_product/"

input_schema.name: mass_action
input_schema.description: Bulk operation to perform from the Actions dropdown: "Delete", "Change status", or "Update Attributes".

input_schema.name: selection_mode
input_schema.description: How to select products before applying mass action. "visible" uses the Select Visible link to select all rows on the current page. "checkbox" selects individual product row checkboxes (at least one) via agentic logic.

input_schema.name: status_value
input_schema.description: Target status when mass_action is "Change status". Ignored for other mass_action values.

input_schema.name: meta_title_value
input_schema.description: Meta Title value to apply on the Update attributes form when mass_action is "Update Attributes". If omitted, Meta Title will not be changed.
